metadata.title: test(rate-limiter): add reproducer for dynamic-binding config-flow investigation
metadata.author: gandhipratik203

description:
## Summary

Adds end-to-end tests that exercise `POST /v1/tools/plugin_bindings` against the gateway HTTP path and validate whether per-tenant binding overrides actually reach the rate-limiter at runtime. Captured as reproducers for the investigation tracked in #4665.

Three lifecycle test methods, each following the same inspection-friendly shape (POST / UPSERT / DELETE walk of the binding's full path through API, Postgres, plugin manager, and Redis):

| Method | Class | Lifecycle phase | Marker | Runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable` | `TestRateLimiterBindingApiEnforcesLimits` | POST happy path — binding is created, persisted, and enforces at the binding's `by_user: 7/m` limit at dispatch | `@pytest.mark.slow` | ~70s |
| `test_upsert_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable` | `TestRateLimiterBindingModeAndLifecycle` | UPSERT — second POST with the same `(team, tool, plugin)` triple updates the existing row in place AND propagates the new mode past the DB into the plugin manager (enforce → disabled flip verified at dispatch) | `@pytest.mark.slow` | ~75s |
| `test_delete_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable` | `TestRateLimiterBindingModeAndLifecycle` | DELETE — binding removal is verified on every write surface it landed on (API + Postgres). No post-delete behavioural burst — the gateway-wide RateLimiter at `by_user: 30/m` plus session-affinity tool-path amplification (~5×–24× ticks per call) makes a post-delete behavioural assertion environment-dependent; structural deletion check is the reliable contract | `@pytest.mark.slow` | ~75s |

Plus shared helpers used by all three: MCP session handshake (now from `tests/helpers/mcp_session.py`), tool team-id stamping via `docker exec psql` (`_stamp_tool_team_id`, fixture-driven), API + DB binding fetch (`_get_binding_via_api`, `_psql_get_binding_config`), live runtime plugin state lookup (`_get_admin_plugin_state`), Redis snapshot (`_redis_rl_keys`).

## Empirical finding from running these against current `main`

Binding payloads that include **gateway-scoped keys** (`redis_url`, `redis_key_prefix`) silently lose their **caller-scoped overrides** (`by_user`, `by_tenant`, `by_tool`) at runtime. Payloads that omit those keys have their overrides applied cleanly.

The deterministic signal is the Redis key window suffix:

| Binding payload contents | Redis key written | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Includes `redis_url` + `redis_key_prefix` (alongside `by_user: "5/s"`) | `rl:<tenant>:user:admin@example.com:60` | `:60` window → static `by_user: 30/m` is enforcing — binding's overrides silently dropped |
| Omits `redis_url` + `redis_key_prefix` (just `by_user: "5/s"`) | `rl:<tenant>:user:admin@example.com:1` | `:1` window → binding's `by_user: 5/s` is enforcing — overrides reach the runtime |

Captured via `redis-cli MONITOR` over multiple runs; reproducible.

## What `test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable` walks through

Run with `-s` to see the inline `[inspect]` phase pointers in real time:

```bash
pytest tests/integration/test_rate_limiter_plugin_bindings_e2e.py \
    ::TestRateLimiterBindingApiEnforcesLimits \
    ::test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable \
    -v -s --with-integration -m slow
```

Seven phases, ~70 seconds total:

1. **Baseline capture** — `GET /admin/plugins/RateLimiterPlugin` to log what's currently mounted in memory.
2. **POST binding** with deliberately uncommon, distinct values for all three dimensions: `by_user="7/m"`, `by_tenant="9/m"`, `by_tool={fast-time-sse-get-system-time: "11/m"}`. Each value is recognisable in API responses, DB rows, and Redis Insight.
3. **Persistence cross-check** — the binding row is fetched both via `GET /v1/tools/plugin_bindings/?binding_reference_id=…` (API) **and** via direct `docker exec psql` against the `tool_plugin_bindings.config` JSON column (DB). Both must return the binding's exact values for all three dimensions.
4. **Pause for inspection** (`PROPAGATION_WAIT + 10s`) — gives the runner time to refresh Redis Insight (still no `rl:*` keys) and DBeaver (binding row visible in `public.tool_plugin_bindings`).
5. **Paced 5-call burst** — calls are sent 3 seconds apart so the counter increments are observable in Redis Insight; each call's outcome (`ALLOWED` / `BLOCKED` / `ERROR`) is printed inline as it happens.
6. **Inspect Redis snapshot** — dumps all `rl:*` keys with their values and TTLs; sleeps another 30 seconds so the runner can compare counter values across `:user:` / `:tenant:` / `:tool:` keys.
7. **Behavioural assertion** — confirms `rate_limited >= 1` (some call was blocked) and that all three dimension counter keys (`:user:`, `:tenant:`, `:tool:`) are present in Redis, proving the binding's multi-dimensional merged config genuinely reached the plugin at runtime.

## What you'll see in Redis Insight during the inspection test

After Phase 4 (filter `rl:*`):

```
rl:<tenant_uuid>:user:admin@example.com:60                          = ~50–100   (ttl 59s → 30s)
rl:<tenant_uuid>:tenant:<tenant_uuid>:60                            = ~50–100
rl:<tenant_uuid>:tool:fast-time-sse-get-system-time:60              = ~50–100
```

All three keys with the same tenant UUID. The exact counter value varies between runs (~5x–20x amplification per call — it's not deterministic), but the **presence of all three dimension keys** is the stable signal.

## What you'll see in DBeaver during the inspection test

```
Phase 1 (~5s in):    new row appears in public.tool_plugin_bindings
                     - binding_reference_id : rl-binding-inspect-<hash>
                     - plugin_id            : RateLimiterPlugin
                     - tool_name            : fast-time-sse-get-system-time
                     - mode                 : enforce
                     - config (JSON)        : {"algorithm":"fixed_window",
                                                "backend":"redis",
                                                "by_user":"7/m",
                                                "by_tenant":"9/m",
                                                "by_tool":{"fast-time-sse-get-system-time":"11/m"},
                                                "fail_mode":"open"}

Phase 7 (~67s in):   row deleted (cleanup_bindings fixture)
```

Crucially: the `config` JSON does **not** include `redis_url` or `redis_key_prefix` — they're absent because we deliberately omitted them from the binding payload (the #4665 finding).

## Caveats / known flakiness

- **Tool-path amplification varies between runs** (~5×–20× ticks per call, depending on cache state, framework internal call patterns, etc.). The lifecycle test's enforcement-transition pattern reflects this:
  - **High-amplification runs**: every call blocks on the very first plugin invocation (`0 allowed / 5 blocked`)
  - **Low-amplification runs**: 1–4 calls slip through before the binding's tight 7/m trips (`1–4 allowed / N blocked`)

  Both shapes are valid; the assertion only requires `rate_limited >= 1`. Phase 6 prints which shape occurred for clarity.
- **Per-tenant manager propagation** across the 3 gateway replicas via Redis pub/sub is not always instantaneous; occasionally one replica still serves the static config briefly after a binding is created. The `PROPAGATION_WAIT` (7s) plus the inspection pause (10s) usually covers it, but it's the same flake any binding test would hit, not specific to this one.

## Status

**Draft.** Investigative artifact for #4665, not production-ready as a gating regression test. Once #4665 lands a fix that locks down the binding-payload shape (rejecting gateway-scoped keys at write time), the inspection test becomes a clean end-to-end regression check.

## Related

- #4665 — investigation issue these reproducers are captured for (rate-limiter-specific binding-config-flow gap + payload hardening)
- #4635 — companion PR refreshing the broader rate-limiter integration + load test suite for current main contracts (independent — this PR doesn't depend on it)

reviews.author: msureshkumar88
reviews.body:
## Test run — all 3 pass ✅

Ran the full suite locally against the docker-compose dev stack (Postgres + 3-replica gateway + Redis) on branch `test/rate-limiter-dynamic-binding-repro`.

```
======================== 3 passed in 240.50s (0:04:00) =========================
```

| Test | Outcome | Key signal |
|---|---|---|
| `test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable` | ✅ PASS | 5/5 calls blocked (HTTP 429); all three Redis dimension keys present (`user`, `tenant`, `tool`) |
| `test_upsert_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable` | ✅ PASS | Upsert to `mode: disabled` → 5/5 calls allowed, no `rl:*` keys written — dispatch correctly skipped |
| `test_delete_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable` | ✅ PASS | DELETE removes binding from API + Postgres; Redis counters expire naturally |

The reproduce signals are solid — the inline `[inspect]` phase output confirmed each lifecycle step at the expected DB, Redis, and behavioural surfaces. Good addition to the investigation corpus.

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): add reproducer for dynamic-binding config-flow investigation

End-to-end test that POSTs a binding via /v1/tools/plugin_bindings,
runs an MCP-session-aware tool burst, and inspects Redis to confirm
whether the binding's per-tenant overrides reached the runtime.

Captured during the investigation for #4665. Empirical observation:
binding payloads that include gateway-scoped keys (redis_url,
redis_key_prefix) silently lose their caller-scoped overrides
(by_user, by_tenant) at runtime; payloads that omit those keys
have their overrides applied cleanly. The deterministic signal is
the Redis key window suffix:

  - :60 (60-sec window) -> static by_user: 30/m is enforcing
  - :1  (1-sec window)  -> binding's by_user: 5/s is enforcing

The test as committed omits the gateway-scoped keys to document
the working path. Some assertions remain flaky (tool-path
amplification + 1-sec window timing can mask the "5 allowed before
blocking" pattern with "all blocked"); the Redis-key-shape signal
is reliable across runs.

Depends on the MCP session-handshake helpers from #4635; this branch
is based on test/rate-limiter-test-infra-refresh and will be rebased
to main once that lands.

Related: #4665
Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): add inspection-friendly multi-dim binding lifecycle test

Adds test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable in
TestRateLimiterBindingApiEnforcesLimits. Marked @pytest.mark.slow so it
doesn't run on default invocations; intended for manual inspection
alongside Redis Insight.

The test walks all three layers of the binding contract for the
RateLimiterPlugin:

  1. Captures baseline runtime config from GET /admin/plugins.
  2. POSTs a binding with deliberately uncommon, distinct values for
     all three dimensions: by_user="7/m", by_tenant="9/m",
     by_tool={fast-time-sse-get-system-time: "11/m"}. Each value is
     easy to spot in API responses, DB rows, and Redis Insight.
  3. Cross-checks persistence: GET /v1/tools/plugin_bindings/ +
     direct docker-exec psql query. Both must return the binding's
     exact values for all three dimensions.
  4. Sleeps for human inspection at three points: pre-binding,
     post-binding-pre-burst, post-burst. Total runtime ~55-60s.
  5. Bursts 5 tool calls via the MCP session-aware path.
  6. Asserts all three dimension counter keys appear in Redis,
     proving the multi-dimensional merged config reached the plugin's
     runtime — not just the user dimension.

Helpers added at module level:
  - _get_admin_plugin_state(plugin_name) — fetches the live runtime
    plugin state from /admin/plugins.
  - _get_binding_via_api(ref_id) — fetches the binding row by its
    binding_reference_id via the gateway API.
  - _psql_get_binding_config(ref_id) — direct docker-exec psql probe
    of the tool_plugin_bindings.config JSON column for a belt-and-
    braces persistence cross-check.
  - _redis_rl_keys() — returns rate-limiter keys with their values
    and TTLs, for inline phase-5 reporting.

Run with -s to see the inline [inspect] phase pointers in real time:

  pytest tests/integration/test_rate_limiter_plugin_bindings_e2e.py \
      ::TestRateLimiterBindingApiEnforcesLimits \
      ::test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable \
      -v -s --with-integration -m slow

Related: #4665, #4674
Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): pace lifecycle test's burst with per-call observation

Replaces the tight loop in Phase 4 with a 3-second-paced burst that prints
each call's outcome (ALLOWED / BLOCKED / ERROR) inline as it happens. Two
benefits:

  1. The counter in Redis climbs visibly — viewer sees ~18 → 35 → 52 → 68 → 97
     across the 15-second burst window instead of jumping to ~75 instantly.
     Makes the rate-limiter's behaviour observable in Redis Insight in
     real time.
  2. The test now demonstrates the *enforcement transition* explicitly —
     first call passes, subsequent calls block once the counter exceeds the
     binding's 7/m limit (with tool-path amplification).

Phase 6 assertion strengthened to require both `allowed >= 1` and
`rate_limited >= 1`, formally pinning the transition pattern.

Total runtime now ~70s (was ~57s); still well under the slow-marker
threshold and only runs with `pytest -m slow`.

Related: #4665, #4674
Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): relax inspection-test assertion to rate_limited >= 1 only

The previously-stronger `allowed >= 1` assertion proved flaky across runs
because tool-path amplification varies between ~5x and ~20x ticks per
call. With binding's tight 7/m by_user limit, the very first call
sometimes already trips (high-amplification runs) — both "1 allowed +
4 blocked" and "0 allowed + 5 blocked" are valid enforcement, the test
shouldn't be picky about which.

The deterministic enforcement signal is rate_limited >= 1 (something
got blocked). Phase 6 still surfaces the per-call narrative in the
inline output for human inspection — the test prints either:

  ✓ visible enforcement transition: N allowed → M blocked
or:
  ✓ enforcement was strict from the first call: all M blocked
    (amplification high this run)

so the runner sees what happened either way, without the test failing
on a brittle timing-dependent assertion.

Related: #4665, #4674
Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): drop redundant tight-user-limit smoke test

test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable already covers the binding
happy-path and adds (a) multi-dimensional Redis-key verification
(user/tenant/tool), (b) API + Postgres persistence cross-checks, and
(c) a paced 5-call burst tuned for session-affinity amplification.

test_binding_with_tight_user_limit_blocks_burst only added a stricter
"first allowed → later blocked" transition shape that's unobservable
under amplification (~24x ticks per user-level call), which made it
flaky on back-to-back runs without giving a unique signal.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): replace delete-binding test with lifecycle-style structural check

test_delete_binding_restores_baseline_dispatch's post-delete-burst
assertion assumed the gateway-wide RateLimiter would not interfere.
With our test config at mode: enforce + by_user: 30/m and session-
affinity tool-path amplification (~24x ticks per user-level call),
the pre-delete burst saturates the per-user bucket and post-delete
calls stay blocked by the gateway-wide limit — not the deleted binding.

Replace it with test_delete_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable, which
mirrors test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable's structure (paced
5-call burst, multi-dim 7/9/11 binding, _say()-instrumented phases).
Phase 7 verifies the deletion via the same API + Postgres write
surfaces the persistence test's phase 2 verifies the POST against —
sidestepping the amplification confound while still asserting the
contract that DELETE removes the binding from every place POST landed it.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): replace disabled+upsert tests with lifecycle-style upsert check

Drop two binding tests that asserted "BURST_SIZE=15 → allowed == 15"
under mode=disabled. The assertion only held because mode=disabled
causes cpex to skip the plugin entirely (no Redis writes, no threshold
checks) so amplification + gateway-wide static limits couldn't trip
them. Test 3 (test_disabled_mode_allows_burst_through) was redundant
with phase 9 of the new upsert test. Test 4
(test_upsert_from_enforce_to_disabled_stops_blocking) is replaced
with a lifecycle-style version that:

  * Asserts the upsert path actually updates the existing row in place
    rather than failing on the (team, tool, plugin) unique constraint
    or creating a duplicate row (API + Postgres cross-check).
  * Verifies the mode field flipped at the API surface (enforce →
    disabled), proving the framework's operator-label echo is stable.
  * Confirms the new mode propagates past the DB into the plugin
    manager via a paced 5-call disabled burst that's unblocked.
  * Mirrors the persistence + delete tests' structure: paced bursts
    sized for session-affinity amplification, _say()-instrumented
    phases, optional human-eyeballing pauses.

Also remove now-dead scaffolding (BURST_SIZE, BURST_LIMIT_PER_SEC,
_send_tool_burst — unpaced 15-burst helper) — only the deleted tests
referenced them.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): default container names to mcp-context-forge-* for reviewer reproducibility

The previous defaults pointed at our development project name
(rl-binding-test-postgres-1, rl-binding-test-redis-1), which only
matched stacks brought up via docker compose -p rl-binding-test up.
Anyone running the standard make compose-up from the repo root gets
mcp-context-forge-* container names — the docker exec calls for
psql / redis-cli would skip silently, leaving a confusing pass-but-
incomplete test result.

Switch the defaults to mcp-context-forge-* (the standard project
name) and document the override path in the comments alongside
PG_CONTAINER and _redis_rl_keys's container var. Behaviour preserved
for callers using a custom project name via the existing env vars
(RATE_LIMITER_TEST_PG_CONTAINER and REDIS_CONTAINER_NAME).

Verified the test still passes against our local rl-binding-test stack
when those env vars are set.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
docs(rate-limiter): expand binding-test docstring with reviewer-friendly setup + run instructions

The previous docstring listed requirements but didn't tell a reviewer
HOW to satisfy them — no mention of `make compose-up`, no full env-var
table, only a single `pytest ...` line that didn't show the inspectable
lifecycle test or the `-s` invocation. New reviewers had to grep the
file to discover override paths (RATE_LIMITER_TEST_PG_CONTAINER,
REDIS_CONTAINER_NAME, etc.).

Replace the 5-line Requirements + 2-line Usage block with:

  - Requirements: same list + the docker exec dependency that wasn't
    previously called out
  - Setup: explicit `make compose-up` step with the project-name caveat
    that drives the container-name defaults below
  - Usage: full-suite invocation AND a `-s -m slow` example for the
    inspectable lifecycle test (with note that they're ~70s each)
  - Environment variables: full table of every override the file reads,
    so reviewers can scan once instead of grepping
  - Notes on flakiness: amplification variability + the
    plugin:RateLimiterPlugin:mode Redis-pollution recovery snippet
    (we hit this repeatedly during development; saves the next person
    that debugging session)

No code changes — pure documentation. All 3 tests still collect.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi

commits.message:
test(rate-limiter): add per-call diagnostic output + autouse Redis isolation to inspectable lifecycle test

Adds two changes that make test_binding_full_lifecycle_inspectable
useful as an operator-debugging tool, not just a CI assertion:

1. Diagnostic output during the burst phase (Phase 4):

   - Phase 1 prints the exact bindings-API POST payload + the response
     body so the wire shape is visible without a separate curl reproducer.

   - Phase 4 prints, for each of the 5 paced calls:
       * the POST URL + headers + JSON-RPC tools/call body
       * the response status + body (200 result OR 429 with cpex's
         "Plugin Violation: Rate limit exceeded" details, including
         dimensions.violated[] and remaining)
       * a Redis counter snapshot for all 3 dimensions (user/tenant/tool)
         taken immediately after the call
       * on 429: the response's `remaining` value plus the implied
         `effective_limit = counter + remaining`
       * a differential verdict — "would the static config (30/m) have
         blocked this call? would the binding (7/m)? observed?" — so
         operators can read the output and convince themselves which
         limit is actually firing per call. Particularly useful on
         call 1 where counter often sits below the static limit but
         above the binding limit, giving an unambiguous "binding's
         tighter limit is what's enforcing ✓" signal.

   The diagnostic markers are deliberately not flagged as TEMP so
   future readers know they're a permanent feature of this test.

2. Autouse Redis-state isolation fixture
   _isolate_rate_limiter_redis_state_between_binding_tests:

   - DELs the gateway-wide `plugin:RateLimiterPlugin:mode` Redis key
     before each test. This key is set by
     tests/integration/test_rate_limiter_dynamic_behavior.py's
     teardown to "disabled" (assuming the static yaml's baseline);
     when present it overrides binding-driven `mode: enforce` at
     per-tenant manager build time (see
     mcpgateway/plugins/gateway_plugin_manager.py
     ::_apply_redis_mode_overrides), silently breaking these tests.

   - Wipes leftover rl:* counter keys so per-call snapshots in the
     diagnostic output start from zero rather than from a stale window.

   - Skips gracefully if Docker / Redis container isn't reachable —
     the suite is already pytest-skipped on a missing gateway via
     _is_gateway_running().

   Mirrors the equivalent isolation fixture pattern in
   tests/integration/test_rate_limiter_multi_tenant.py
   (_isolate_rate_limiter_between_tests).

Verified: test passes against a long-running gateway stack with
deliberately-seeded stale `plugin:RateLimiterPlugin:mode = "disabled"`
in Redis — the autouse fixture clears it and call 1 gives the clean
"binding's tighter limit is what's enforcing" diagnostic line.

Signed-off-by: Pratik Gandhi <gandhipratik203@gmail.com>
commits.author: Pratik Gandhi
